panels.title: Dataset freshness (expected vs actual)
panels.description: Catches the case where every upstream job reports SUCCESS but the underlying business data is actually stale (plan §9's motivating example).

targets.rawSql: SELECT ds.dataset, p.pipeline_id, (p.sla_json->>'freshness_target_minutes') AS target_minutes, round((ds.freshness_s / 60.0)::numeric, 1) AS actual_minutes, ds.row_count, ds.updated_at, CASE WHEN (p.sla_json->>'freshness_target_minutes') IS NULL THEN 'no target' WHEN ds.freshness_s / 60.0 > (p.sla_json->>'freshness_target_minutes')::float THEN 'STALE' ELSE 'FRESH' END AS status FROM dataset_state ds LEFT JOIN pipeline p ON p.outputs_json @> jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('iceberg', ds.dataset)) ORDER BY ds.dataset

panels.title: Freshness over time (minutes since last snapshot)
panels.description: Trend of the 'freshness' dimension's observed value (minutes since last update) per dataset over the last 6h, from dq_result - shows whether a dataset is drifting stale gradually or jumped suddenly.

targets.rawSql: SELECT evaluated_at AS time, dataset, observed / 60.0 AS freshness_minutes FROM dq_result WHERE dimension = 'freshness' AND evaluated_at > now() - interval '6 hours' ORDER BY evaluated_at
